oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

slot.description: The scene of its launch-grid slot, when it sits in one.

oneOf.description: In the launch grid, at the intersection of the track and a scene.
In the arrangement: a placement of the whole clip from `start` (in ticks).

Command.description:
A Faulk command, `{"type": "domain.verb", ...}`. One variant per domain; the
domain's enum holds its commands.

DeviceCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Set a parameter of a device, by the parameter's id, in the unit the device
declares. The parameter must be one the device has and the value must be finite;
the engine clamps it to the parameter's range. The built-in synth's parameters:
`waveform` (0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 triangle), `attack`, `decay` and
`release` (seconds, 0.002 to 30), `sustain` (0 to 1), `gain` (0 to 1, linear).
Undo: set the parameter back to its previous value.

DeviceId.description: Identifier of a device in a track's chain.

HistoryCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Undo the last entry of the history: one command, or every command of one
history group. Does nothing when there is nothing to undo; refused while a
group is open. Undo: `history.redo`.

Open a history group: every edit of the same author until `history.end_group`
becomes one entry, undone at once (a mouse drag). Refused when a group is
already open (groups do not nest). Undo and redo are refused while it is open:
the host ends it when the gesture or the turn ends. Not undoable itself.

Close the open history group. Refused when no group is open, or when another
author opened it. Not undoable itself.

oneOf.description:
Start a note on a track's instrument. `note` is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127
(60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a note off. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.note_on` on the same track. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Release every playing note on every track (panic button). Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

oneOf.description:
Set a track's volume in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value outside
the range or not a number is refused. A fader gesture sent in one history group
is undone in one step. Undo: set the previous volume back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Set a track's pan, from -1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside the range or
not a number is refused. A pan gesture sent in one history group is undone in
one step. Undo: set the previous pan back.

Mute or unmute a track. Mute is saved with the project and versioned. Undo: set
the previous state back.

Set the master's volume in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value
outside the range or not a number is refused. Undo: set the previous volume
back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

Note.description:
A note: a value without an id (CT-4). Its order compares fields in declaration order:
(start, pitch, length, velocity, cents, chance, repeat).

The last three fields are optional in the file: a default value is not written, and an
absent one reads as the default, so a note has exactly one representation. `chance` and
`repeat` are stored and edited here; the clip player reads them with #192.

cents.description: Fine tuning in cents, -50 to 50 (0 by default).

chance.description: Probability that the note plays, in percent, 0 to 100 (100 by default).

repeat.description: How many times the note repeats, 1 to 16 (1 by default).

start.description: Position from the start of the clip, in ticks.

NoteChange.description: A note to replace by another: `clip.notes.update` addresses a note by its whole value.

from.description: The note as it is in the clip now.

length.description: Length on the timeline, in ticks.

offset.description: Where in the clip the placement starts, in ticks, before the clip's length.

start.description: Start in the arrangement, in ticks.

oneOf.description:

"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement

is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the

identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:

when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what

`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

Note.description:

(start, pitch, length, velocity, cents, chance, repeat).

absent one reads as the default, so a note has exactly one representation. `chance` and
`repeat` are stored and edited here; the clip player reads them with #192.

chance.description: Probability that the note plays, in percent, 0 to 100 (100 by default).

start.description: Position from the start of the clip, in ticks.

from.description: The note as it is in the clip now.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

ClipSnapshot.description: A MIDI clip as `clip.restore` brings it back (everything but its identifier).

launch_quantize.description: A per-clip launch quantization, when one was set (the MVP never sets one).

slot.description: The scene of its launch-grid slot, when it sits in one.

oneOf.description: In the launch grid, at the intersection of the track and a scene.
In the arrangement: a placement of the whole clip from `start` (in ticks).

oneOf.description:
Set a parameter of a device, by the parameter's id, in the unit the device
declares. The parameter must be one the device has and the value must be finite;
the engine clamps it to the parameter's range. The built-in synth's parameters:
`waveform` (0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 triangle), `attack`, `decay` and
`release` (seconds, 0.002 to 30), `sustain` (0 to 1), `gain` (0 to 1, linear).
Undo: set the parameter back to its previous value.

DeviceId.description: Identifier of a device in a track's chain.

HistoryCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Undo the last entry of the history: one command, or every command of one
history group. Does nothing when there is nothing to undo; refused while a
group is open. Undo: `history.redo`.

Open a history group: every edit of the same author until `history.end_group`
becomes one entry, undone at once (a mouse drag). Refused when a group is
already open (groups do not nest). Undo and redo are refused while it is open:
the host ends it when the gesture or the turn ends. Not undoable itself.

Close the open history group. Refused when no group is open, or when another
author opened it. Not undoable itself.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters). Undo: `clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: same name, colour, length, loop
and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot of the same track: `slot` when given (it must be free),
otherwise the next free slot below the source's scene. Refused, with no effect,
when the track has no free slot to give. A second placement of the same clip is
an option of the arrangement commands, not of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of
the copy.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name clears it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Undo: set the length back, restoring what
`trim` cut.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused). Undo: set the previous content back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

oneOf.description:
Set a parameter of a device, by the parameter's id, in the unit the device
declares. The parameter must be one the device has and the value must be finite;
the engine clamps it to the parameter's range. The built-in synth's parameters:
`waveform` (0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 triangle), `attack`, `decay` and
`release` (seconds, 0.002 to 30), `sustain` (0 to 1), `gain` (0 to 1, linear).
Undo: set the parameter back to its previous value.

oneOf.description:
Undo the last entry of the history: one command, or every command of one
history group. Does nothing when there is nothing to undo; refused while a
group is open. Undo: `history.redo`.

Open a history group: every edit of the same author until `history.end_group`
becomes one entry, undone at once (a mouse drag). Refused when a group is
already open (groups do not nest). Undo and redo are refused while it is open:
the host ends it when the gesture or the turn ends. Not undoable itself.

Close the open history group. Refused when no group is open, or when another
author opened it. Not undoable itself.
